lyrics:
[Intro: chugging acoustic guitars, congas, nonsense syllables]
Doo-da-lee, doo-da-lee-dee
Doo-da-lee, doo-da-lee-dee

[Chorus: two voices in close harmony]
We see you there, Miss Abernathy
The kettle's on for more than only you
(Ooh, ooh, ooh)
Stay as you are, Miss Abernathy
The avenue is leaning on you
(Hey, hey, hey)

[Verse 1: quick, sly, guitars and bass]
She taught the whole of Elm Street how to find a middle C
She kept a tin of buttons and a list of who owed tea
She knew which kids were hungry and she never said a word
Just left a plate, and nobody heard

[Chorus: two voices in close harmony]
We see you there, Miss Abernathy
The kettle's on for more than only you
(Ooh, ooh, ooh)
Stay as you are, Miss Abernathy
The avenue is leaning on you
(Hey, hey, hey)

[Verse 2: quick, wistful]
Where did they go, the ones who knew our names?
The milkman and the crossing guard, the man who fixed the trains
The lady at the library who saved the book for you
The street is asking, and it's overdue

[Verse 3: slower, guitars soften]
The van came on a Thursday and the piano went downstairs
She waved from the back window like a queen with other cares
She left the tin of buttons on the wall beside the gate
We shared them out, we stayed up late

[Final Chorus: two voices, fuller, tambourine]
So long, so long, Miss Abernathy
The kettle's on, it's on for only you
(Ooh, ooh, ooh)
Go as you are, Miss Abernathy
The avenue will try to carry through
(Hey, hey, hey)

[Outro: guitars and nonsense syllables, fading]
Doo-da-lee, doo-da-lee-dee
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 92 BPM, 4/4, F-sharp major. A light, chugging folk-rock shuffle. Wry on the surface and wistful underneath.

VOICE: Two men singing in very close harmony, one high and pure, one lower and drier, so tightly matched that they sound like one voice with two edges. The verses are delivered quickly and lightly. Nonsense syllables at the start and end.

INSTRUMENTS: Two acoustic guitars strummed percussively, one playing a chugging low-string figure. Congas. Electric bass. A light drum kit with brushes. Tambourine. A soft electric guitar adding small fills.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, guitars, congas and syllables. 0:12 Chorus. 0:34 Verse 1. 0:54 Chorus. 1:16 Verse 2. 1:36 Verse 3, slower and softer. 2:00 Final chorus with changed words. 2:24 Outro, guitars and syllables fading by 2:50.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Late-1960s New York folk-rock: crisp, dry and close, acoustic guitars bright, the two voices blended and centred.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The turn at 1:16, when a song about one woman suddenly asks where everyone like her has gone.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The watchers in the original are cold and the woman is being managed. Here the watchers are grateful neighbours, and the vanished heroes are local. It is the view of people who now are the old ones on the street.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Affection, a wider sadness, a fond farewell.
